dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: svavad anyaśarīre 'pi saṃvittim anubhāvayet | apekṣāṃ svaśarīrasya tyaktvā vyāpī dinair bhavet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
sanskrit_variants: verse 107: GRETIL encoding artefact '=B9' restored as avagraha: anyaśarīre 'pi.
dharana.rendering: Let one feel awareness in another's body just as in one's own; letting go of concern for one's own body, one becomes all-pervading within days.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: a body is not necessary for consciousness; in dream one is conscious apart from the gross body, in deep sleep apart from the subtle body, and in the fourth state apart from the causal body. Knowing this, one contemplates one's consciousness as not confined to one's own body. Wallis: 'cultivate the felt-sense that the consciousness in another's body is the same as one's own'.
dharana.technique_name: The Same Awareness in Another's Body
dharana.instruction: Feel awareness alive in another person's body just as in your own.

checked_against: The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 83' = verse 107 (agrees with Singh)
Wallis concordance: verse 107 = 'Becoming all-pervasive (Y82 ~ B3)' (verse text and technique match)
GRETIL, Wallis and Pradīpaka: Sanskrit of verse 107 compared
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.mystery_within_parallel: The parallel-translations section of The Mystery Within labels verse 107 'Dharana 84', because from verse 106 on it gives every verse its own number (106 = 83 … 137 = 114). Singh and the same book's Session Two list put this at dhāraṇā 83. Not followed.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 107 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the same awareness felt in another's body
concern for one's own body released
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is awareness felt in one's own body and then, just as vividly, in another's.
geometry.svg_hint: two simple figures; the glow at the centre of one is mirrored in the other
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Feel it in another
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: awareness that seems shut inside one body is felt just as much in another's. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn attention toward what the verse names, and let everything else stay in the background
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: Awareness felt in another person's body as vividly as in one's own
attention.secondary: Releasing preoccupation with one's own body

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Let one feel awareness in another's body just as in one's own; letting go of concern for one's own body, one becomes all-pervading within days.
adiyogi.method_summary: Feel the awareness alive in your own body. Then bring to mind someone nearby, or a person you know, and feel the same awareness alive in their body, just as vividly. Let go of concern for your own body for a while.

honesty.disclosure: Door 083 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 83 (verse 107) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 083 is dharana 83, verse 107. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Stay respectful: this is an inner contemplation, never a reason to cross anyone's physical or emotional boundaries. The verse's 'within days' is its own claim, not a promise. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
